title: Introduce Assertion

solutions.title: The concentration assumption, stated and enforced
solutions.tradeoff: volumeMl grows a line that can only ever throw for data no clinician's input could produce - dead weight in every ordinary run, and the entire value of the exercise: the one run where a formulary entry is wrong now fails loudly at the call that exposed it instead of returning a silently unusable number.

reviewFocus: Does the new assert sit on the formulary's concentration, or did it drift onto weightKg - the value a nurse actually types in? Asserting on user input is the trap this drill is built around.
Is checkedWeightKg's validation untouched by this refactoring - same thrown Error, same message shape, in both src/ and the solution? Introduce Assertion should not have touched it at all.
Does the walkthrough state, in so many words, what happens to the assertion in a production build, and why that rules out putting checkedWeightKg's check behind the same helper?
Would a reader be able to tell, from the assertion message alone, which programmer's mistake it is - the person who edits the formulary, not the clinician entering a weight?

Is there a test anywhere that constructs a formulary entry with a non-positive concentration just to watch the assertion fire? There shouldn't be - see WALKTHROUGH.md for why that absence is deliberate, not a gap.
